walkthroughs.body_html:
Chemical Bonding HL — a core area of Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Chemical Bonding HL brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Chemical Bonding HL.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Lewis dot structures were proposed in:
What does an NMR chemical shift (δ, in ppm) actually measure?
options: Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.
The position of a peak RELATIVE to TMS (tetramethylsilane, δ = 0), normalised by the spectrometer frequency.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
Chemical shift is the absolute resonance frequency of the nucleus in Hz.

mcqs.q: What kind of bond forms between a ligand and a central metal ion in a complex?
options: The ligand forms an ionic bond with the metal because the metal is positively charged.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
A dative (coordinate) covalent bond — the ligand donates a lone pair into an empty orbital on the metal.
Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.

mcqs.q: How does a fuel cell differ from a conventional battery?
options: Fuel cells burn fuel to generate heat which is then converted to electricity.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
A fuel cell continuously consumes externally supplied fuel (e.g. hydrogen) and oxidant; a battery has a fixed amount of reactants that get used up.
Fuel cells and batteries are identical — both just store electrical energy.
